findings.current: “Still, our side did give you some valuable information, didn’t we?”
findings.defect: The draft omits 하나, changing one specific valuable piece of information into an unspecified amount.
findings.rationale: 하나 explicitly specifies one item of information.
findings.replacement: “Still, our side did give you one valuable piece of information, didn’t we?”
findings.source: 그래도 저희 쪽에서 귀한 정보도 하나 드렸잖아요?

findings.current: Wolhwa narrowed her eyes at his shamelessly evasive answer.
findings.defect: The draft generalizes Jin Wikyung’s deliberate pretense of knowing nothing into mere evasiveness, losing the specific characterization cue.
findings.rationale: 시치미를 떼다 specifically means to feign ignorance or pretend not to know.
findings.replacement: Wolhwa narrowed her eyes at his answer, delivered as though he knew nothing.
findings.source: 시치미 뚝 뗀 대답에 월화가 눈을 가늘게 떴다.

findings.current: “What’s gotten into you? Every time someone says something like that, you’re the one who lectures them about dignity and propriety.”
findings.defect: The draft introduces an indefinite speaker and object, making Wipeng someone who lectures anyone who speaks this way rather than someone who habitually lectures Jin Wikyung.
findings.rationale: The immediate exchange and Jin Wikyung’s familiar 자네 establish his own prior remarks and Wipeng’s lectures to him as the subject of the complaint.
findings.replacement: “What’s gotten into you? Whenever I say something like that, you’re always lecturing me about dignity and propriety.”
findings.source: 자네가 웬일인가? 이런 말을 할 때마다 체통이니 뭐니 따분한 잔소리만 하던 위인이.

findings.current: “You’re really making an occasion of this today. What is it? Tell me already!”
findings.defect: “Making an occasion of this” is unnatural and obscures Jin Wikyung’s amused observation that Wipeng has deliberately committed to flattering or indulging him today.
findings.rationale: 작정했군 means that Wipeng has evidently made up his mind to pursue this behavior in earnest.
findings.replacement: “You’re really going all out today. What is it? Tell me already!”
findings.source: 자네 오늘 작정했군. 뭔가? 어서 말해 보게!

findings.current: “The Third Young Master absolutely cannot be let off the hook. It wasn’t enough for him to leave at a time like this as if none of it concerned him—the moment he left, all word from him stopped.”
findings.defect: The draft adds the unsupported claim that contact stopped at the exact moment he left.
findings.rationale: 소식이 뚝 끊겼어요 says that all news has abruptly or completely ceased, but does not identify the precise moment when that happened.
findings.replacement: “The Third Young Master absolutely cannot be let off the hook. It wasn’t enough for him to leave at a time like this as if none of it concerned him—on top of that, all word from him has completely stopped.”
findings.source: 이런 시기에 나 몰라라 나간 것으로도 모자라서 소식이 뚝 끊겼어요.

findings.current: Of them, Woo Hwangtae, the chief of the Seongun Escort Bureau, was in the worst state by far. Thanks to his worthless son, he was frantic.
findings.defect: The neutral word “frantic” strips out the deliberately crude, comic register of 똥줄이 타다.
findings.rationale: 똥줄이 타다 is a vulgar colloquial expression for suffering extreme anxiety or impatience; the source intentionally contrasts that register with Woo Hwangtae’s status.
findings.replacement: Of them, Woo Hwangtae, the chief of the Seongun Escort Bureau, was in the worst state by far, shitting himself with worry thanks to his worthless son.
findings.source: 그들 중에서도 못난 아들 덕분에 한창 똥줄이 타고 있는 성운표국의 국주, 우황태는 그 정도가 더욱 심했다.

findings.current: “Come now, man. What do you mean? I’m the chief of the Seongun Escort Bureau, remember?”
findings.defect: “Remember?” implies that the guard was previously told and has forgotten, while the Korean emphatically insists on Woo Hwangtae’s identity without that implication.
findings.rationale: 라니까 marks emphatic insistence—“I’m telling you”—rather than a request to remember.
findings.replacement: “Come now, man. What do you mean? I’m telling you, I’m the chief of the Seongun Escort Bureau!”
findings.source: 어허, 이 사람아. 그게 무슨 소리인가? 나 성운표국 국주라니까?

findings.current: Like Woo Jintae, he had lived comfortably beneath the halo of his family.
findings.defect: “Lived comfortably beneath the halo” is an unnatural calque and weakens the point that he actively enjoyed the substantial advantages of his family’s prestige.
findings.rationale: 후광을 톡톡히 누리다 means to benefit substantially from reflected status or influence.
findings.replacement: Like Woo Jintae, he had always enjoyed every advantage of his family’s prestige.
findings.source: 우진태와 마찬가지로 가문의 후광을 톡톡히 누리며 살았던 그다.

findings.current: *Those bastards. No matter how powerful they are, how can they treat someone like this?*
findings.defect: The draft sanitizes the violent profanity in 쳐 죽일 놈들.
findings.rationale: 쳐 죽일 놈들 is substantially stronger than the unmodified “bastards” and reflects Woo Hwangtae’s furious internal voice.
findings.replacement: *Those fucking bastards. No matter how powerful they are, how can they treat someone like this?*
findings.source: 쳐 죽일 놈들. 제아무리 위세가 높다지만 사람을 이렇게 푸대접해?

findings.current: *I ought to just take this merchant down.*
findings.defect: The draft invents a completed intention to “take down” Woo Hwangtae and removes the source’s deliberately unfinished, exasperated threat.
findings.rationale: The Korean trails off after 확, preserving an unspoken impulse rather than specifying a concrete action.
findings.replacement: *This damned merchant, I ought to just…*

findings.current:
“Look at this cow-brained bastard! You there, stop!”

The giant’s body trembled.

“What did you just say?”

“I called you cow-brained. You son of a bitch, you’re lower than a cow!”
findings.defect: The draft changes the repeated physical comparison “ox-headed” into an insult about intelligence and renders the giant’s sudden flinch as sustained trembling, weakening the specific trigger and reaction behind the confrontation.
findings.rationale: 소대가리 같은 literally compares his head to an ox’s, and the phrase is deliberately repeated after 움찔 describes a brief involuntary flinch.
findings.replacement:
“You ox-headed bastard! Stop right there!”

The giant flinched.

“What did you just say?”

“I called you ox-headed. You bastard, you’re worse than an ox!”
findings.source:
“이런 소대가리 같은 놈을 봤나! 너 거기 안 서!”

그때, 거한이 몸을 움찔 떨었다.

“지금, 뭐라고?”

“소대가리 같은 놈이라고 했다. 이 소만도 못한 새끼야!”

findings.current: Baek Museong, Huashan’s Lone Crane, had restrained his junior brother just before he exploded. He smiled at Woo Hwangtae.
findings.defect: “Restrained” can imply physical restraint, but Baek Museong stops his Junior Brother with the spoken prohibition immediately preceding this sentence.
findings.rationale: 만류하다 means to dissuade or stop someone from acting; no physical restraint is described.
findings.replacement: Baek Museong, Huashan’s Lone Crane, had stopped his Junior Brother just before he exploded. He smiled at Woo Hwangtae.
findings.source: 폭발하기 직전의 사제를 만류한 화산일학(華山一鶴) 백무성은 우황태를 향해 빙긋 웃어 보였다.

summary: The draft is broadly faithful, but it omits one quantity, alters several pragmatic and temporal cues, softens vulgar register, and changes the repeated ox-head insult that triggers the final confrontation.
